newsitem.title: CANADA: Pan-Alberta plucks new president from producers.
newsitem.headline: Pan-Alberta plucks new president from producers.

text.p: Pan-Alberta Gas Ltd, the Canadian natural gas aggregator currently under fire from some of its producer pool members, said on Thursday it appointed a new president from the ranks of the producing community.
Pan-Alberta, which is in the midst of coming under full control of NOVA Corp, said it named for Suncor Inc vice-president Ross Weaver to head the operation.

Pan-Alberta markets natural gas for a pool consisting of over 400 gas producers. It is one of three operations in an impending split-up of Novagas Clearinghouse, owned by Calgary-based NOVA and NGC Corp of Houston.

Two weeks ago, a heavyweight group of producers, including such firms as Anderson Exploration Ltd, PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd and Talisman Energy Inc, filed a lawsuit against Pan-Alberta, claiming the aggregator since 1992 breached contractual and fiduciary obligations by not selling pool gas for the highest possible price.
The suit was the latest in a series of moves showing producer dissatisfaction with NOVA and its subsidiaries.

Pan-Alberta on Thursday said Weaver, who was most recently Suncor's vice-president of marketing, brings to the position much marketing, business development and risk management experience in the North American gas industry.

Last week, NOVA and NGC said they agreed in principle to reorganize Novagas Clearinghouse in a transaction that would include NOVA taking full control of Pan-Alberta and Novagas's midtream gas and gas liquids assets. NGC will assume gas marketing activities, replicating the company's operations in the United States.
